hypotheses.observation: Policy-window sample counts rise from 30,049 (r2-users5) to 37,550 (r2-users10) to 47,404 (r2-users20) in windows that each span 300,000 ms (to_epoch_ms minus from_epoch_ms in the window summaries), while jmeter_active_threads held exactly 5, 10, and 20 for the whole of each window (min = max, standard deviation 0). Samples grow about 1.6x while users grow 4x.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: In this closed workload, per-request response time may grow as load rises (throughput per user falls), or pacing/think-time settings may shape the scaling; a throughput-limiting bottleneck is also possible but is not established by these counts.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the raw JTL data to compute per-window latency percentiles for each stage and compare them. Rising latency with users supports response-time growth; flat latency with saturating throughput would point to pacing configuration instead.

hypotheses.observation: frontend cpu_cores is nearly flat across stages: mean 0.1818516 (r2-users5), 0.1893414667 (r2-users10), 0.1881028 (r2-users20), with per-window maxima 0.196647, 0.199595, and 0.198735 cores, while window sample counts increase about 1.6x from the 5-user to the 20-user window.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The frontend may be running against a CPU quota near 0.2 cores (for example a container CPU limit) that caps its utilization; alternatively its per-request CPU cost may be small relative to fixed overhead. This is a hypothesis only — no CPU limit is stated in the evidence.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the frontend's configured CPU limit or quota for a value near 0.2 cores; in a rerun, collect frontend CPU throttling metrics to test whether the frontend is capped at higher loads.

hypotheses.observation: paymentservice memory_bytes mean rises across stages: 32,281,941.6 (r2-users5), 33,451,281.1 (r2-users10), 33,689,645.5 (r2-users20), with the r2-users20 max at 33,796,096 and a much tighter spread there (IQR 82,432 versus 1,210,709 at r2-users5). frontend memory_bytes mean also rises: 11,957,407.3, 12,937,261.5, 14,036,150.0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Heaps may be warming toward a steady state (caches filling) or approaching a ceiling as load rises; a slow leak is possible but cannot be distinguished from warm-up by three 300,000 ms windows.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun a longer fixed-load soak and compare the memory slope across windows: a plateau suggests warm-up, while a continuing climb warrants heap or garbage-collection inspection.

hypotheses.recommended_check: If edge behavior matters, inspect raw JTL samples whose timestamps fall outside the three windows; otherwise treat every window verdict as scoped to its own window only.
